verdict.headline: NFP loses 23,000 jobs — September hike thesis collapses as equities close at records
verdict.label: Labor shock resolved rate-hike risk but not supply-shock risk: SPX 7,757 record, 30Y holds 5.17%, gold surges $110, Hormuz unresolved
verdict.rationale_short: July payrolls printed −23,000 against an 80,000 consensus, with May and June revised down a combined 103,000 and average hourly earnings cooling to +3.2% YoY. September hike odds on Kalshi collapsed from 54% to 36% — 34 points below the 70% trigger. Equities rallied to records (SPX +0.62%, Nasdaq +1.30%), but the 30Y eased only 3bps to 5.17% and gold surged +2.61% to $4,350: two cross-asset signals that the inflation-growth tension is unresolved. Khamenei has still not responded to the Hormuz draft; oil held near its regime thresholds. Level that changes the read: 30Y closes below 5.00% on two consecutive sessions, or SPX closes below 7,380.

trade_setups.thesis: Khamenei has not publicly responded to the restrictive Hormuz draft. The structure has a 3% vs 5-7% transit fee gap between Oman's offer and Iran's ask. Pezeshkian described communication as 'very difficult at the moment.' A negotiated deal (3% transit fee): Brent drops toward $74-75, both oil triggers clear, and the 30Y has a path toward 5.00%. Restrictive draft approved (US/Israeli ship ban): Brent clears $85 and WTI clears $79 simultaneously — the dual breach that held the regime at 3-of-6 earlier this cycle. The deal has failed to close three times in 2026; each miss was followed by an oil recovery from the dip.
trade_setups.entry: Brent $82.15 and WTI $78.31 are $2.85 and $0.69 from their respective breach thresholds. Brent holding below $79 for two sessions after any Khamenei announcement signals a workable modification rather than the restrictive version.
trade_setups.invalidation: Khamenei approves the restrictive draft; Brent clears $85 and WTI clears $79 — regime widens from 1-of-6 to 3-of-6 at Monday open.

trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y eased only 3bps to 5.17% on the largest NFP miss of 2026. That limited response confirms the long end is pricing the Hormuz oil premium as much as the rate path. July NFP −23K plus AHE +3.2% YoY removed the wage-inflation channel; August 13 CPI tests whether the supply-inflation channel has attenuated similarly. July CPI embeds the June-July oil prices ($82-91/bbl) before the recent pullback. Below 3.0% on CPI: 30Y has a direct path through 5.00%, the sole formal breach resolves, and the full rate-relief thesis is confirmed. Above 3.5%: 30Y holds 5.17%+ regardless of labor data.
trade_setups.entry: Current: 5.17%. Formal threshold: 5.00%. Two consecutive closes below 5.00% extinguish the sole remaining regime breach — the most consequential market event of the next five trading days.
trade_setups.invalidation: CPI above 3.5% on August 13 validates Kashkari's supply-shock thesis; September hike odds recover above 55%; 30Y holds 5.20%+.
trade_setups.horizon: August 13 CPI as primary catalyst; Hormuz resolution as secondary.

trade_setups.thesis: NVDA held the $216-221 range through the SpaceX Vera Rubin commitment and the NFP session. At ~$221, the Q2 FY27 earnings (August 26) need gross margin above 76% and a Q3 guide above consensus. The SpaceX $15.83B AI capex commitment is real demand and raises the guide floor — but it also raises what 'good enough' looks like at current prices. AMD −8% AH on a genuine beat from $518 and DDOG −17% on beat-and-raise from 25-30x NTM are the recent templates: altitude amplifies the response to any disappointment. The Jackson Hole keynote begins August 27 — one day after earnings — with no de-risk window between them.
trade_setups.entry: Support: $216 (structural, held through SpaceX news and NFP session). Resistance: $222-225. Two closes above $225 through CPI would suggest the market is pricing a clean August 26 beat.
trade_setups.invalidation: Two consecutive closes below $210 on normal volume before August 26 would imply the AMD post-earnings pattern is extending.

bear_case: The −23K NFP print is not a soft labor market — it is actual job losses, with three consecutive months of downward revision (May, June, now July) that make the reported-jobs baseline through 2026 materially weaker than the tape priced. Gold at $4,350 and equities at records on the same day is the stagflation correlation: gold is pricing deteriorating real growth alongside persistent supply-driven inflation, not just rate relief. The 30Y at 5.17% — down only 3bps after the largest NFP miss of 2026 — confirms the bond market has not accepted the full 'no hike, no inflation' thesis. If August 13 CPI prints above 3.5% with oil still at $82 and Khamenei unresponsive, Kashkari's supply-shock frame (hike into labor softness because the inflation is supply-side) becomes the dominant policy read. A record SPX at 7,757 with −23K jobs and $4,350 gold is pricing rate relief, not growth; if 30Y does not clear 5.00% by August 15, that pricing is vulnerable. If SPX retreats below 7,380, the record-close bid is not holding.
